summary: Tower still standing about 10 km north of Wawa, Ontario; a hobby list gives it a second name, and the two sources disagree on whether its cupola is gone.

facts.status_note: Still standing with no cupola on top, per a Firelookout.ca directory note; the hobby list does not mark it as a cupola removal.

evidence.supports: Location: about 10 km north of Wawa and about 2 km west of Catfish Lake
evidence.quote: Located approximately 10km North of the town of Wawa, ON, and 2km West of Catfish Lake.

evidence.supports: Tower still standing with no cupola on top (directory note)
evidence.quote: The tower is still standing, with no cupola on top.

evidence.supports: Writer did not reach the tower before dark and was unsure of its condition
evidence.quote: I was unable to make it all the way to the tower before dark, so not sure of many other details of its condition at this time.

evidence.supports: Listed on the still-standing list as Menzies/ Bailloquet Tower at Catfish Lake, Wawa, with no cupola-removal star
evidence.quote: 10- Menzies/ Bailloquet Tower- Catfish Lake, Wawa, Ont.

evidence.supports: Star legend: a star marks a cupola removal
MNR decided as of 2013 to remove many still-standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

evidence.supports: MNR no longer maintains the listed towers; visitors asked not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

evidence.supports: MNR has removed the bottom section of ladder on these towers
evidence.quote: that is why the MNR has removed the bottom 20 ft of ladder

evidence.supports: Hobby website set up to preserve fire lookout history and towermen
evidence.quote: I decided I would produce a website to preserve the history of our fire tower lookouts and the towermen that worked them.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The directory calls it Catfish Lake Fire Tower; the list calls it Menzies/ Bailloquet Tower. Both place it at Catfish Lake near Wawa, so the list is probably the same tower, though it gives no reason for the second name.

The directory note says there is no cupola; the list gives no star, which marks a cupola removal. The list is dated as of 2013 and the directory note is undated, so the two may describe different times.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History (home page)

notes_for_editor: Thin record: only a Firelookout.ca directory entry (no dates, heights or design) and a hobby site's list dated about 2013. No build date, height, design, staffing, or access level found; access is omitted because no source says whether the land is public. The brief has no local_unit and no source I read gives a district. WebSearch is US-only, so only websearch.py was used; it returned no government, archive or newspaper page on this tower. Follow-up: Forest History Ontario archives, MNR fire records, and Wawa municipal history.
